summary: An excerpt from Book 11 (part 109) of a novel, apparently Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm style fiction, where Rebecca Randall and Emma Jane trade banter about a mortgage that is depicted as a villain in a sketch. The conversation turns to Rebecca's future career as a writer or editor and to whether she should become a missionary to Syria, which she declines because she does not feel a call. The girls then debate whether God can reach heathen peoples who have not been sent missionaries.
one_line: Rebecca Randall and Emma Jane joke about a mortgage sketch, then debate Rebecca's career and whether missionaries are needed for the heathen.
key_facts: Rebecca Randall sketches the mortgage as a fiend or ogre holding an axe uplifted in his red right hand.
The sketch shows a tiny house on the right with a weeping family gathered in front of it.
Rebecca says the mortgage in the sketch is only a twelve hundred dollar mortgage, which she calls a small one.
Rebecca says John once saw a man mortgaged for twelve thousand dollars.
Emma Jane asks Rebecca whether she shall be a writer or an editor.
Emma Jane suggests Rebecca go out as a missionary to Syria, as the Burches keep urging her to.
Rebecca says the Board would pay the expenses of a missionary to Syria.
Rebecca says she cannot make up her mind to be a missionary and does not feel a call, as Mr. Burch says one must.
Rebecca says she would like to do something for somebody and make things move, but does not want to teach people how to live when she has not learned herself.
Emma Jane argues that if everyone who ought to go to save the heathen stays home, they will not be saved.
Emma Jane says God must always be present, ready and waiting, and cannot move about and miss people.
Emma Jane says God will make allowances for heathen living in hot climates, where parrots, tigers, snakes and bread-fruit trees distract their minds.
Emma Jane says heathen without books cannot think as well but will find God somehow, some time.
Emma Jane's question to Rebecca is 'What if they die first?'
